note: Ravina and Rabba Tosefa'a were walking on the road when they saw a man drawing water with a bucket during the intermediate days of a Festival. Rabba Tosefa'a urged Ravina to excommunicate him. Ravina pointed to a teaching that one may draw for vegetables in order to eat them. Rabba Tosefa'a answered that the word there means pulling out crowded vegetables, not drawing water. Ravina then cited a teaching that says explicitly that one may draw water for vegetables, and Rabba Tosefa'a accepted it and withdrew his view.
why: The Gemara has just quoted a teaching that one may water vegetables during the Festival week in order to eat them but not to improve them; the story is an argument over what that teaching's word for drawing means.

people.name: Ravina
people.about: He defends the man drawing water, citing a teaching that permits it.

people.name: Rabba Tosefa'a
people.about: He wants the man excommunicated, then retracts when shown an explicit teaching.

terms.meaning: The days between the first and last days of Passover and Sukkot, when some work is permitted but heavy or unnecessary labor is not.
To place a person under a ban, cutting him off from the community, as a penalty for defying the Sages.
A teaching of the early Sages that was not included in the Mishna, the core text the Gemara discusses.

note: During the intermediate days of a Festival, the Bedita River overflowed and left large numbers of fish on its banks. Everyone went, caught fish and brought them home, and Rava permitted them to salt some of them. Abaye objected that one may preserve only food one can eat during the Festival. Rava replied that since they had brought the fish home intending to eat them, and the fish would spoil if left unsalted, they count as goods about to be lost, and salting them is permitted.
why: The mishna allows preserving only foods that can be eaten during the Festival week; this case tests that rule when far more fish arrived than could be eaten, and the discussion goes on to give a second version of Rava's ruling.

people.name: Rava
people.about: He permits the townspeople to salt the fish and defends the ruling.

people.name: Abaye
people.about: He challenges Rava's ruling from the mishna.

terms.meaning: The days between the first and last days of Passover and Sukkot, when some work is permitted but unnecessary labor is not.
The core early teaching of Jewish law that the Gemara discusses and explains.
A category of work allowed during the Festival week to prevent a financial loss that could not be avoided otherwise.
